chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Marry off the foolish man and do not marry off the foolish woman, for the foolish man begets (children who are useful) and the foolish woman does not beget (useful children).
ai.seo_question: Why should one marry off a foolish man but not a foolish woman according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the social utility of marrying a foolish man (*al-ahmaq*) versus a foolish woman (*al-hama’*), noting that men are primarily valued for their ability to procreate and provide, while women’s role in child-rearing requires greater cognitive capacity. This reflects the traditional Shia jurisprudential view that marital suitability is assessed through the lens of *maslaha* (public interest) and the specific capacities required for the roles of father and mother within the family structure.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from the one who narrated it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘(one may) marry to the stupid man but do not marry the stupid woman, for the stupid man would beget (children who would contribute to the society) but the stupid woman would not beget (will have worthless children)’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from those who narrated to him who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
You can give in marriage to a dimwitted man but do not marry a dimwitted woman; a dimwitted man can have children (healthy ones) but a dimwitted woman cannot.”’
